subject: DPA: telemetry access workflow and cross-border handling
messages:
From: Emma Zhao <emma@clienthealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClientHealth SSQ follow-up: telemetry, access controls, cross-border

Michael / team,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Legal and our privacy ops are reviewing the DPA annex and the security questionnaire (SSQ). Two asks we need to close before procurement can move forward:

1) A tidy telemetry dataflow diagram that shows where raw request/response telemetry is stored, how long it's retained, and which subprocessors (if any) can access it.
2) A matrix listing roles with access to telemetry and the conditions for access (SRE, Support, Audit), plus proof of how access is logged and reviewed (sample audit entry would be great).

We also need clarity on cross-border handling: if we route inference requests through Dedicated instances in the us-west region, are there any hops or backups that could send telemetry metadata to eu or apac regions (even for failover)? If so, we need details for our DPA transfer annex.

Can you share the diagram and a short note on access controls and retention? We would like to close this by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Zhao
Lead Security Program Manager, ClientHealth
ops+privacy@clienthealth.com

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Emma Zhao <emma@clienthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ClientHealth SSQ follow-up: telemetry, access controls, cross-border

Emma — thanks, and great questions. Attaching a compact diagram and an access matrix export to start (see attachments). High level: we separate production inference telemetry into two buckets:

- Ephemeral request telemetry (per-request metadata, token counts, timing) — kept for 72 hours by default and used for routing/healthing. Pseudonymized at ingest (request IDs only; no PII persisted).
- Persistent observability artifacts (aggregates, anomalies, sampling traces) — kept up to 180 days depending on the retention policy you select under the account settings. These artifacts are stored in our us-west region for your account by default.

Access control summary (also in the attached ssq-access-matrix.xlsx):
- Support: can view aggregated dashboards; no direct raw request playback. Access is role-provisioned and requires two-step approval for elevated playback.
- SRE/On-call: have ephemeral access via jumpbox with session recording. All sessions are logged to immutable audit logs.
- Security/Compliance: read-only access to archived bundles; exports require approval and are tracked with ticket IDs.

Cross-border: for Dedicated and Private customers we pin compute and telemetry storage to the specified region. Failover paths that cross regions are opt-in: we do not enable automatic cross-region failover for telemetry without prior configuration. If you select cross-region backups, those transfers are listed in the DPA transfer annex and use encrypted transit and at-rest protections; we can provide a list of subprocessors involved in backups.

Attached: redwood-telemetry-dataflow-v2.png, ssq-access-matrix.xlsx. I will follow up with the DPA excerpt on transfers (we have a short summary PDF).

Best,
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood-telemetry-dataflow-v2.png (image/png)
Attachment: ssq-access-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ClientHealth SSQ follow-up: telemetry, access controls, cross-border

Emma — quick clarifying points from an operational perspective.

On Wed, Sep 21, 2027 at 11:03 AM Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com> wrote:
> Attached: redwood-telemetry-dataflow-v2.png, ssq-access-matrix.xlsx. I will follow up with the DPA excerpt on transfers (we have a short summary PDF).

Two operational items to call out explicitly so your audit team can see them:

- Runbook gating: any support or SRE playback that could show request-level content requires a ticket in our internal system (linked to a customer support case). The request to enable playback is reviewed by Security and must include justification and time-bounded scope.
- Audit proof: we can export a sample immutable audit entry (redacted) showing who requested playback, the ticket id, timestamp, and the MFA-enabled session id that was used. We avoid exporting actual request payload in that sample for privacy.

I'll prepare the sample audit entry and a short paragraph describing the runbook flow and attach by tomorrow. Karthik — can you confirm we have a DPA-ready line to add about optional cross-region backups and the subprocessors used for long-term archival?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Emma Zhao <emma@clienthealth.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ClientHealth SSQ follow-up: telemetry, access controls, cross-border

Emma / team — from a legal perspective I want to confirm the wording we'll put into the DPA transfer annex regarding optional archival backups and subprocessors.

Proposed redline (summary): 
"Redwood will store ClientHealth telemetry within the region designated at account onboarding. Optional long-term archival backups may be stored in secondary regions solely at Customer's written instruction. Any cross-border archival transfers will be documented in the DPA transfer annex and carried out with industry-standard encryption in transit and at rest; Redwood will provide a list of subprocessors and transfer routes on request."

If that language looks correct to you, Michael/Marissa please add the short PDF (dpa-crossborder-summary.pdf) that summarizes the subprocessors and encryption controls. Also, Emma, to make procurement move quickly we can add a DocuSign envelope for the DPA addendum; please confirm the email address you want the envelope sent to.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
Attachment: dpa-crossborder-summary.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks everyone — the diagram and matrix are very helpful. A few quick confirmations before we sign:

- ClientHealth will request optional cross-region archival only if our internal residency policy requires multi-region redundancy. The DocuSign envelope should go to legal@clienthealth.com.
- Please include the redacted audit sample (Marissa mentioned) in the loop so our auditors can close the evidence item.
- We also want a one-page runbook summary that we can attach to the procurement ticket describing the playback approval flow.

If you can send the three items (DocuSign, sample audit entry, one-page runbook) by Monday morning our procurement team will finalize the PO. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Emma
Emma Zhao
Lead Security Program Manager, ClientHealth
